classification: Project method implications explicitly inferred from named source distinctions; not empirical results

items.distinction: Body and soul are separate enquiries; constitutional temperament is not silently a psychological type.
The same translated motion family has competing or ambiguous direction explanations.
items.effect_on_project: Require source-specific motion semantics before compilation, rather than sharing an unexamined helper.

items.distinction: Mars appears in a conditional speech-relief branch as well as injurious ones.
items.effect_on_project: Retain both polarities within their antecedents; no globally harmful Mars switch.

items.distinction: Appearance, social reproach, treatability, cure, concealment, public visibility and material benefit are distinct outputs.
items.effect_on_project: Later outcome coding must match the claimed dimension; no counting benefit from illness as no illness.

items.distinction: Honourable placement is not moral goodness. Contrary placement is not absence of every talent or virtue.
items.effect_on_project: Do not force all descriptor signs to follow a single dignity sign.

items.distinction: The fifteen single/pair cases are conditional profiles selected in a topical scheme, not fifteen independent aspect tests.
items.effect_on_project: No additive per-adjective evidence, no plain conjunction lookup, and no five-planet profile substituted for the full source method.

items.distinction: Commentary, lexical senses, manuscript omissions and table scope must remain attributed.
items.effect_on_project: Do not promote a translator’s detailed explanatory checklist as a direct author instruction.

items.distinction: Similar condition labels can be repeated in different source topics.
items.effect_on_project: Treat their dependence explicitly; source repetition is not a new observed case or validation trial.

items.distinction: The historical sex-role discussion changes primary significator and contains moralized categories.
items.effect_on_project: Preserve historical meanings but provide no current identity or clinical classifier.
